name: Wildflower
description: Yousef has a rooted tree$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ consisting of exactly $$$n$$$ vertices, which is rooted at vertex $$$1$$$. You would like to give Yousef an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$, where each $$$a_i$$$ $$$(1 \le i \le n)$$$ can either be $$$1$$$ or $$$2$$$ . Let $$$s_u$$$ denote the sum of $$$a_v$$$ where vertex $$$v$$$ is in the subtree$$$^{\text{†}}$$$ of vertex $$$u$$$. Yousef considers the tree special if all the values in $$$s$$$ are pairwise distinct (i.e., all subtree sums are unique). Your task is to help Yousef count the number of different arrays $$$a$$$ that result in the tree being special . Two arrays $$$b$$$ and $$$c$$$ are different if there exists an index $$$i$$$ such that $$$b_i \neq c_i$$$. As the result can be very large, you should print it modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A tree is a connected undirected graph with $$$n - 1$$$ edges. $$$^{\text{†}}$$$The subtree of a vertex $$$v$$$ is the set of all vertices that pass through $$$v$$$ on a simple path to the root. Note that vertex $$$v$$$ is also included in the set.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ $$$(1 \le t \le 10^4)$$$ — the number of test cases. Each test case consists of several lines. The first line of the test case contains an integer $$$n$$$ $$$(2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — the number of vertices in the tree. Then $$$n−1$$$ lines follow, each of them contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ $$$(1 \le u,v \le n, u \ne v)$$$ which describe a pair of vertices connected by an edge. It is guaranteed that the given graph is a tree and has no loops or multiple edges. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print one integer $$$x$$$ — the number of different arrays $$$a$$$ that result in the tree being special , modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2117F — Wildflower [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
